title: Eval runbook for automated batching/caching configuration changes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Short summary: Create a reproducible evaluation runbook and automation to validate quality regressions introduced by automated batching and KV-caching recommendations. The goal is to be able to safely apply cost-saving configurations at scale with automated acceptance checks and deterministic rollback triggers.
motivation: We want to expose per-customer batching/caching recommendations to reduce token costs but must ensure no user-visible quality regression. Prior experiments showed small but meaningful hallucination and context-truncation risk under certain cache shapes and batch windows.
success_criteria:
1) A CI job that runs a golden-prompt eval suite against every batching/caching profile change and produces a pass/fail decision within 30 minutes.
2) Automated guardrail that prevents rollout or triggers rollback if acceptance thresholds are exceeded.
3) Dashboards surface per-model/per-prompt metric deltas and run history.
4) Documentation and runbook for SRE/SE to handle edge cases.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline in GH Actions or internal runner that: spins up recommendations config, deploys to canary subset (5% traffic), runs golden-prompt evals, computes thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim/qual labels), and emits verdict.
- Thresholds are configurable per-model and stored in config-store.
- Rollback automation integrated with rollout controller; manual approval path available.
- Alerts wired to PagerDuty and Slack channel #runtime-rollouts for failures.
design_notes: We will use deterministic golden prompts covering five buckets: API-formatting, instruction-following, factuality, hallucination-prone queries, and long-context continuity. Each bucket has 8 prompts. Metrics: token-level divergence (embedding cosine vs baseline), scalar quality labels from a lightweight classifier, and human spot-check rate. The pipeline computes both absolute deltas and relative z-scores against a rolling baseline.
implementation_plan:
1) Define golden-prompt sets and baseline runs for models in catalog.
2) Implement eval harness that can be run against variants: different batch sizes, batching timeouts, KV cache hit/miss simulation, cache population policies.
3) Add GH Action and internal scheduler to run on every config change PR and before canary rollout.
4) Integrate results with rollout controller to gate apply/rollback.
5) Add dashboards and incident runbook.
run_steps:
- Pre-PR: run local harness on sample dataset, attach artifacts.
- On PR: CI runs full eval; summary artifact uploaded to S3 and linked.
- Canary deploy: controller deploys config to 5% traffic and re-runs eval against production-like traffic for 2 hours.
- Decision: auto-apply to more traffic if pass; auto-rollback and page on fail.
golden_prompts_strategy: Design guidelines: brevity for deterministic scoring, mix of open-ended and constrained prompts, edge-case factualities that historically regress under batching. Each prompt is annotated with expected outputs and scoring function. Prompts live in repo under /golden-prompts/{model}/{bucket}.jsonl.
metrics_and_thresholds: Primary metrics: embedding-cosine-drop (threshold per-bucket default 0.03), classifier-failure-rate (default 2%), token-level perplexity-delta (model-specific), and percentage of exact-match commands (for structured output). Failure rules combine metrics: any embedding drop > threshold AND classifier-failure-rate increase > baseline*1.5 should fail the eval.
rollback_policy: Automated rollback triggers: fail verdict from eval pipeline, user-reported degradation with >5 incidents in 1 hour, or latency SLO breaches tied to batching changes. Rollback preserves original config and emits a postmortem ticket template. Rollbacks are incremental: first revert canary, then stop rollout, then full rollback if no improvement.
observability: Dashboards: per-model eval history, per-prompt deltas, top failing prompts, rollout timeline, and cost-savings estimate. Logs: capture request traces, batch composition, cache hit/miss events with keys anonymized. Alerting: fail-eval -> P0; degrade-quality but within soft thresholds -> P2 to #runtime-ops.
tests_and_evals: Unit tests for harness, integration tests for controller gating, synthetic adversarial tests to simulate cache poisoning, and monthly human review on a sampled set. Add A/B evals comparing cost-savings against user-visible metric degradation at 90/95 percentile traffic.
security_and_privacy_considerations: Golden prompts must not contain PII or customer data. Eval runs against production traces must be redacted; use hashing for request identifiers. Config store access requires RBAC: only release engineers and product owners can adjust thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false negatives where regressions don’t appear in golden prompts. Mitigation: enlarge prompt set periodically, include sampled production queries in nightly regressions, and add live canary monitoring. Risk: overfitting thresholds to historical data; mitigation: use holdout windows and conservative safety margins.
open_questions:
- Should the CI evaluator run full-scale KV-cache population or use a simulator?
- What percentage of traffic is safe for initial canary for high-risk models (LLMs with critical factuality)?
- Which stakeholders sign off on threshold changes (PM + ML + Runtime lead)?

review_feedback: Priya (ML): "Classifier threshold needs per-model calibration; avoid one-size-fits-all."
Omar (PM): "Include a cost-benefit calculator so product owners can weigh marginal savings vs. quality risk."

notes: This ticket focuses on the safety and observability surrounding automated cost optimization suggestions, not on the optimization algorithm itself. Implementation should be modular to support future knobs like quantization or kernel swapping.
